hypothesis_statement: In highly popular/widely-watched fixtures, short-priced home favourites (bookmaker consensus implied probability > 65%) are systematically overpriced relative to their true win probability.
economic_or_market_rationale: Public betting volume skews toward popular favourites; bookmakers may shade prices to balance books rather than to reflect fair probability.
required_features: fixture popularity/TV coverage flag, bookmaker consensus, exchange closing price
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED — research candidate only, not a trading signal.

hypothesis_statement: Markets where bookmaker consensus shows high dispersion (wide IQR) at T-24h see systematically larger subsequent price movement toward one side than low-dispersion markets.
economic_or_market_rationale: Disagreement among bookmakers may reflect genuine uncertainty about team news/form not yet priced in uniformly, which resolves as information arrives closer to kickoff.
required_features: T-24h bookmaker odds snapshot, closing bookmaker/exchange odds
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED — research candidate only, not a trading signal.

hypothesis_statement: When exchange back price remains materially above bookmaker consensus implied probability within 30 minutes of kickoff, that gap contains genuine value rather than noise.
economic_or_market_rationale: Late-moving information (team news, weather) may be reflected on liquid exchanges faster than in some bookmakers' prices, but a persistent gap close to kickoff suggests the market has settled rather than being a transient artefact.
required_features: near-kickoff exchange price snapshots, bookmaker consensus
in_sample_period: not applicable — requires forward data collection
notes: UNVALIDATED. Requires manual near-kickoff price capture — no historical dataset exists yet.

hypothesis_statement: Home advantage is systematically overestimated by bookmaker consensus when the away team has had 3+ days more rest than the home team, and underestimated when the home team has just returned from a long-distance away trip (European away legs).
economic_or_market_rationale: Standard home-advantage priors may not adequately adjust for fixture congestion and travel fatigue, which affects some teams more than others.
required_features: fixture rest-day gap, distance travelled for away legs, European competition calendar
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED — research candidate only, not a trading signal.

hypothesis_statement: Lower-liquidity competitions (Championship, Scottish Premiership) show larger bookmaker price dispersion than Premier League/Champions League, but any apparent edge is substantially eroded by worse exchange execution quality (wider spreads, thinner order books).
economic_or_market_rationale: Less market attention -> less price discovery -> wider dispersion, but the same thin markets likely have poor executable liquidity, so apparent EV on paper may not be realisable in practice.
required_features: bookmaker dispersion by competition, exchange available size at price
test_method: descriptive backtest comparing paper EV to realistic fill assumptions
notes: UNVALIDATED. This hypothesis is partly a warning about liquidity risk, not just an edge to find.

behaviour_name: large late market moves carry information
hypothesis_statement: A late (within 2 hours of kickoff) exchange price move of more than 10% in implied probability predicts the outcome better than the pre-move consensus, beyond what the move itself trivially implies.
economic_or_market_rationale: Large late moves often reflect team-news leaks (confirmed lineups, late injuries) not yet reflected in static bookmaker consensus models.
required_features: near-kickoff exchange price time series, confirmed lineup timestamps
in_sample_period: not applicable — requires forward data collection
notes: UNVALIDATED. Requires manual near-kickoff price capture.

hypothesis_statement: Matches where surface-specific Elo disagrees with bookmaker consensus by more than 8 percentage points of implied win probability identify systematic mispricing in the direction of the surface-Elo estimate.
economic_or_market_rationale: Bookmakers may under-weight surface-specific form relative to overall ranking/form, especially early in a surface season (e.g. clay swing).
required_features: surface-specific Elo ratings, bookmaker consensus, tournament surface
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED. Requires a surface-Elo model, which does not exist yet (Stage 4).

hypothesis_statement: Underdogs (bookmaker consensus implied probability < 35%) with a surface-specific rating within 100 Elo points of their opponent are systematically underpriced relative to true win probability.
economic_or_market_rationale: Public perception and overall ranking may anchor bookmaker prices more than surface-specific current form, especially for players who are notably stronger on one surface than their overall ranking suggests.
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED. Requires a surface-Elo model, which does not exist yet (Stage 4).

hypothesis_statement: Players returning from a layoff of 8+ weeks (injury or otherwise) are systematically mispriced by bookmaker consensus in their first 1-3 matches back, in a direction that is not consistent (i.e. this hypothesis expects to find either persistent over- or under-pricing, and treats 'no consistent direction' as a valid falsification outcome).
economic_or_market_rationale: Ranking-based and Elo-based priors decay slowly and may not adequately capture short-term match-fitness uncertainty after a long layoff.
required_features: player layoff history, match-by-match odds and results post-return
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED — research candidate only, not a trading signal.

hypothesis_statement: Favourites (bookmaker consensus implied probability > 60%) who have played 3+ matches in the preceding 7 days underperform their priced probability relative to less-congested favourites.
economic_or_market_rationale: Fatigue from recent match load may not be fully reflected in bookmaker consensus, which likely weights ranking/surface/form more heavily than very recent schedule congestion.
test_method: backtest vs market-only baseline, then out-of-sample
notes: UNVALIDATED — research candidate only, not a trading signal.

behaviour_name: bookmaker dispersion as uncertainty signal (not value)
hypothesis_statement: High bookmaker dispersion in tennis match-winner markets predicts higher outcome uncertainty (closer to a coin flip) rather than predicting which side is undervalued — i.e. dispersion is a risk signal, not a directional edge signal.
economic_or_market_rationale: Unlike H-FB-002 (which treats dispersion as directionally predictive), this hypothesis explicitly tests the competing, more conservative explanation: that dispersion just reflects genuine uncertainty with no exploitable direction. Both hypotheses are kept in the registry deliberately so the research process doesn't only look for confirming evidence of a directional effect.
test_method: descriptive backtest correlating dispersion with outcome uncertainty
notes: UNVALIDATED — deliberately framed as a risk-signal hypothesis, not a value hypothesis.
